evidence: src/grow/size.ts; dotfiles 2.20/1.17, vite 3.11/2.05, linux 3.99/2.41 height/reach at island radius 2

decision: camera frames the stage (tallest tree on the island), not the tree on show; desktop reserves side column and a typical title width
why: per-tree framing cancels size differences; panel content would otherwise change the scale

decision: pinned folder zoom floor follows the tree on show (capped at the stage), not the stage
why: with the stage floor a sapling folder barely zoomed in; keeps pre-change pin zoom

decision: spin fps comparison inconclusive; triangles equal (16.8k vs 16.5k)
why: shared 4-core box at load 6-18 with other agents; base runs ranged 9.6-16.2 fps, after 9.4-10.6

decision: traced load and spin with scripts/trace.mjs, 5 runs each
why: playbook step 1: attribute long tasks to call stacks before fixing
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/baseline/summary.json; medians longest dotfiles-low 310, linux-low 276, vite-low 355, vite-high 341 ms; spin 41.0/26.8/27.2/9.8 fps
result: every load task over 50 ms is a sync wait on the GPU process: GPU context creation (2D canvas for the contact texture, then WebGL getContext), and shader links at the first frame and at the first tree frame; spin is GPU-process bound (CrGpuMain 97-99% busy, renderer main 10-14%)

decision: draw the contact-shadow gradient into a DataTexture instead of a 2D canvas
why: mantra 1 (don't do it): the 2D canvas started a second GPU context, CommandBufferProxyImpl::Initialize 127-189 ms inside the startup task
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/f1/summary.json vs baseline, 5 runs each: startup task 296->244 ms dotfiles, 277->278 linux; sum of tasks over 50 ms 655->469 dotfiles, 607->459 linux; canvas pixel diff max 1/255 at low and high
result: kept: about 150 ms less blocking per load; context creation cost moved to getContext, so the longest task barely moves

decision: compile every program at startup with compileAsync and hold frames until a fence passes
why: mantra 5 (when they're not looking): link programs while the worker grows the tree
result: rejected: SwiftShader has no KHR_parallel_shader_compile, the fence passes before ANGLE finishes linking, so the first draw waited on every program at once; compiling during generation also competes with the worker for the 4 CPU cores

decision: same, but query one program per task so each wait covers one link
why: split the link waits under 100 ms each
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/f2b/summary.json: longest 706 dotfiles, 872 linux; first query waits 690-790 ms
result: rejected: the command buffer is FIFO, so the first query waits for every compile queued before it, and single SwiftShader links still take 100-260 ms

decision: rebased onto main with the island and tree sizes; re-measured spin with GPU-process CPU per frame
why: wall-clock fps swings 2x on the shared sandbox, CPU per frame does not
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/abl/linux-low-2.txt (runtime ablation, one page, 3 rounds): 154 ms/frame; nothing drawn 60; labels hidden 132; sky hidden 114 (earlier run); UI hidden 125
result: the island added fill; sky quad, labels and tree each cost 20-30 ms of GPU-process CPU per frame

decision: paint the sky as the container's CSS gradient behind a transparent canvas; the sky quad draws only into PNG snapshots
why: mantra 1 (don't do it): the full-screen sky pass filled every pixel on the software GL each frame, while the browser rasters a CSS gradient once
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stem.tsv, linux low, 3 interleaved runs: 158 -> 140 ms/frame GPU-process CPU, 23.0 -> 25.8 fps; screenshots scratchpad/pr7/shots/*: at most 0.016% of pixels differ, all at label edges

decision: draw each label stem as its own element stretched by transform instead of a pill pseudo-element sized by a custom property
why: mantra 1: resizing the stem inside the pill repainted the pill every spin frame
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stem.tsv, linux low, 3 interleaved runs: 140 -> 132 ms/frame, 25.8 -> 27.8 fps

decision: link the tree and island programs one per task at startup from stand-in meshes
why: mantra 5: link while the worker grows the tree
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-warm.tsv, 4 runs: longest 561 -> 1028 ms linux low, 559 -> 1008 dotfiles low; the first link query after startup waits about 1 s
result: rejected: same FIFO wait the 2026-11-03 compileAsync attempt hit

decision: hold the cover, bark and leaves back one frame each on the first tree, so a frame links at most one new program
why: mantra 3 (do it less at once); a growing tree starts collapsed, so the hold does not show
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stage.tsv, 4 interleaved runs: longest 889 -> 492 ms linux low, 862 -> 476 dotfiles low
result: kept; each link still takes 300-600 ms on SwiftShader, so the 100 ms target is out of reach while GL runs on the main thread

decision: new run for PR 12 (CI weather); rows before this one are from earlier runs
why: decision log is shared across PRs

decision: weather thresholds over the last 20 finished runs: storm at 3 failures in a row from the newest; rain when the newest failed or at least 3 failures that are half the runs; cloudy for any other failure; sunny when all passed; clear when none
why: owner asked for sunny/partly cloudy/rain/storm/no CI; a streak reads as broken now, scattered failures as flaky

decision: ask the API for status=completed as well as branch and per_page=20, and count only success vs failure/timed_out/startup_failure
why: in-progress runs would otherwise crowd out finished ones; cancelled and skipped runs say nothing about health

decision: a 404 from the runs endpoint is no CI (clear sky); 403, 429, other errors and the network mean no weather and no chip
why: the tree already proved the repo exists, so 404 means Actions is off; weather must never become an error screen

decision: worker posts the branch as soon as it knows it (cache hit or repo info) so the runs request starts beside the tree download; samples and links with a branch start at once
why: parallel with the tree without a second repo-info request against the 60/hour limit

decision: clouds, sun and lightning hang on a backdrop fixed to the camera 60 units out, behind the tree; rain and snow fall in world space around the island and stop on it
why: owner said never hide the tree behind clouds; a world-space ring of clouds would sit in front of it at some spin angles

decision: weather moves in vertex shaders from one time uniform; moving weather renders every frame like spin, no 30 fps cap
why: a half-rate cap would read as 30 fps in auto quality's 2 s check and step quality down with spin off; spin already renders every frame by default

decision: reduced motion freezes weather at a fixed time with no lightning; tab hidden relies on requestAnimationFrame pausing
why: flashes are a photosensitivity risk; rAF already stops in hidden tabs and dt is capped at 0.1 s on return

decision: weather setting is not in share links; wx= is a preview param that the setting overrides
why: share links carry palette and colorBy only, not ground/spin/labels; turning weather off should be absolute

decision: sample runs are hand-written: vite 20 green runs (sunny), dotfiles and linux no runs (clear); make-runs.mjs added to regenerate them
why: api.github.com is blocked in this sandbox; dotfiles and linux have no .github/workflows in their sample trees

decision: clouds rebuilt smaller and rounder (icosahedron detail 1, softer shading) after first screenshots read as crumpled rocks
why: first pass looked like boulders, not clouds

decision: snow drew nothing; rewrote the snow branch of the fall vertex shader as a plain if and fixed a reversed smoothstep
why: winter storm screenshot showed no flakes while uSnow=0 drew quads

decision: raindrops at low cut from 450 to 260 (medium 650, high 1200) and cloud faces turned from the camera dropped (storm triangles 21.2k to 19.5k)
why: rain and storm cost 13-17% of spin fps on SwiftShader at first

decision: weather journey: goto with a ?visit= query instead of hash plus reload
why: a hash-only goto then reload raced the old repo's replaceState and reloaded acme/limited (applyLink dispatches settings before the load, which rewrites the hash to the shown repo; pre-existing)

decision: sheet drag lives in side.ts with pointer events; content takes touch-action pan-down at scrollTop 0 and pan-y below it
why: lets the browser scroll content natively and hands only a downward drag from the top to script, without touch-event preventDefault
evidence: probe via CDP touch: content swipe up scrolled 190px and stayed open, swipe down at top closed

decision: release snaps by flick first (|v|>0.45 px/ms over the last 100 ms), else by 72 px or 30% of travel toward the other state
why: a quick short flick must decide; a short slow drag should spring back
evidence: e2e short slow 40px stays closed, 40px flick opens and closes

decision: reframe skips while #side has data-dragging and a MutationObserver reruns it when the drag settles
why: a ResizeObserver reframe mid-drag would slide the tree under the finger, and a drag-open leaves the body size unchanged so nothing else fires
evidence: scratchpad/pr13/phone-2-mid-drag.png keeps the closed framing; phone-3-open.png reframed above the sheet

decision: sun is one ShaderMaterial mesh (12 rays, halo, glow, core) moved in the vertex shader from the weather time uniform; sunny and cloudy count as animated
why: three MeshBasicMaterial discs were static and cost three draws
evidence: perf vite low sunny draw calls 7 to 5; scratchpad/pr13/sun-strip.png shows rays turning and halo breathing

decision: ray alpha raised 0.30 to 0.36 after the first strip
why: rays read as barely there against the warm sky at 2x

decision: no frame throttle for the sun-only animation
why: spin is on by default so most sessions already render every frame; cloudy already rendered every frame; rAF stops in hidden tabs
evidence: spin-off sunny idles at 16-21 renders/s on SwiftShader

decision: pr14 history backend run begins; earlier rows are from other runs (up to 2026-11-04T01:30:50Z)
why: new run on branch pr14-history

decision: history core is sampled tree snapshots: ~50-80 commits found with /commits?until= (weekly 26 weeks, monthly to 2 years, yearly before, plus the root), each read with /git/trees/{tree}?recursive=1 and diffed by blob and tree sha
why: owner direction: one request per commit cannot scale (Linux has 1.3M commits); snapshots cost roughly the same for any repo and give last-changed, churn, born, gone and dead wood

decision: per-commit detail only for the newest 100 non-merge commits (DETAIL_COMMITS), giving exact recent dates, commit counts and author attribution
why: precise recent activity and owners without spending the hourly budget on old commits

decision: snapshots processed newest to oldest with a per-path accumulator [newest, oldest, version-oldest, churn, sha]
why: the head tree comes first, so the sample count and the head path set are known before any old tree is read, and contiguity needs no stored previous tree

decision: truncated recursive trees (over 100k entries or 7 MB) are re-read per top-level folder, reusing any top-level subtree whose sha matches the newer snapshot without a request; a split budget caps this and further truncated snapshots are skipped and marked partial
why: Linux's head tree is over 100k entries; reuse keeps the split cost to the folders that changed

decision: long jobs run as resumable steps: each request advances one bounded step (STEP_REQUESTS subrequests, STEP_ENTRIES tree entries), progress lives in KV, the reply is {status:pending, progress} until ready
why: a free Worker allows 50 subrequests and 10 ms CPU per request; steps are deterministic, so two polls racing on one step write the same state

decision: no lock on job state; KV last-write-wins and steps are idempotent, so a race only repeats work. Durable Objects would serialize it but tie the core to Cloudflare
why: keep the core host-agnostic and simple

decision: per-IP cap of 10 new (uncached) repos an hour in KV; cached repos unlimited; the [[ratelimits]] binding holds every IP to 60 requests a minute
why: owner direction: fairness and abuse guard; KV is eventually consistent so it is a guard, not an exact count
evidence: server/src/worker.ts takeQuota; test/worker.test.ts caps new repos

decision: a spent GitHub budget answers pending with retryAfter at the reset, not an error, and the job resumes from KV
why: owner direction: the client shows a calm growing state, and no work is lost
evidence: server/src/core/service.ts errorReply; test waits for the token budget

decision: cron prewarm: one job step for one PREWARM repo every ten minutes, round robin, using GITHUB_TOKEN only
why: owner direction: keep popular repos warm; one step per tick stays inside one invocation's subrequest limit

decision: superseded the single server token: visitors sign in with a GitHub OAuth App (no scopes); an uncached computation runs on the visitor's bearer token for that request only, never stored or logged; signed-out visitors get cached history or {status:needs-auth}
why: owner direction: one shared token does not scale; results come from public data so sharing them in KV is safe

decision: a GitHub 401 is an unauthorized reply with nothing written; /repos/{o}/{r} is now always read so private repos answer error private and nothing about them is stored; the negative cache for missing repos was dropped
why: a bad token must not poison the cache, and a 404 cached from one visitor could hide a repo from another
evidence: server/src/core/service.ts lookUp; tests refuses a token, never computes a private repo

decision: the token returns to the app by postMessage from a popup callback page addressed to the origin saved with the state, instead of a redirect back with the token in the URL
why: keeps the token out of every URL and history entry, and leaves the app's own hash link (repo and settings) untouched; state is single-use in KV for ten minutes
evidence: server/src/core/oauth.ts; test signs in through a popup

decision: the browser-run core with a pasted personal token (coordinator item 3) is not built
why: superseded by OAuth sign-in; the core still takes an injected fetch and Store, so a browser runner for private repos is a later, separate change

decision: sample histories are generated, not hand-written: wrangler dev ran the real Worker against scripts/fake-github.mjs over full-history blobless clones, with each branch head pinned to the commit whose tree matches the bundled fixture
why: api.github.com is blocked here but github.com git clones work; the same code path a visitor hits made the files
evidence: server/scripts/save-history.mjs; dotfiles b7c7894, vite b3cb057, linux 05441d6
result: dotfiles 36/36 and vite 2916/2916 fixture files matched

evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/5ac5cb95-dc76-5c12-add7-5b8ab67deeec/scratchpad/pr14/e2e-transcript.txt; regression test answers probes from the kept listing

decision: older truncated snapshots are kept rather than skipped: paths after the last listed one are assumed unchanged for that interval (git lists recursive trees in path order); the head is always split so the file table is complete; gap snapshots-skipped removed
why: one request per snapshot keeps Linux near the flat budget; skipping lost most recent history for any repo over 100k entries
evidence: server/src/core/job.ts readSnapshot and fold tailAfter; test keeps truncated older snapshots

decision: job state bounded: no rows for folders missing from the head, no new deleted-file rows once GONE_CAP is filled (snapshots are read newest first), shas stored as 12 characters
why: KV values cap at 25 MiB and every step rewrites the state

decision: Linux rerun after the fix: one request hung about 50 minutes inside local workerd (both servers idle); cancelled it and the job resumed from KV at 0.48 and finished
why: the resumable design was meant for exactly this; the hang looks local (large KV write through wrangler's Node loopback), not confirmed
result: ready: 65 snapshots from 2005-04-16, 97359 files, gap tree-truncated, about 380 requests

decision: bundled torvalds-linux.history.json.gz (854 KB gzip, 8.1 MB raw) beside the dotfiles (1.7 KB) and vite (49 KB) histories; a test checks each covers exactly its tree fixture's files
why: samples must work offline; Linux is the large-repo case later features need
